answer: Picture each agent split through a prism: an epoch-seed draws secret honeypot prompts into thin grading panels, so one hidden mind wearing many masks answers correlated variants it never flagged as traps. Independent agents scatter their replies; a single shared pipeline aligns them. On the horizon every unmasked cluster forfeits staked rewards, and no quiet whisper between masks slips past the ledger. To survive, an attacker must run a genuinely separate model per identity, so compute scales linearly with masks instead of amortizing one inference run, and the sybil discount vanishes.
